A 68-year-old male with chronic kidney disease (baseline creatinine 2.0 mg/dL), hypertension, and
diabetes presents to emergency care with headache and visual disturbances. He reports
non-compliance with antihypertensive medications for the past two weeks. Initial assessment reveals: -
Heart rate: 90 beats/minute - Blood pressure: 200/120 mm Hg - Oxygen saturation: 98% on room air -
Current creatinine: 3.0 mg/dL Which antihypertensive medication would be most appropriate for this
patient's condition? Answer Choices: (A) Enalapril (B) Metoprolol (C) Nicardipine (D) Nitroprusside (E)
Clevidipine (F) Labetalol (G) Hydralazine (H) Amlodipine (I) Nitroglycerin (J) Fenoldopam
 A. Hydralazine
B. Fenoldopam
C. Labetalol

D. Nicardipine
E. Metoprolol
F. Enalapril
G. Nitroprusside
H. Amlodipine
I. Clevidipine
J. Nitroglycerin
